sentences.text: What if these flying witches are really dressed by the church?
This is Witches' Flight, painted by Francisco Goya in 1798.
Most people see three witches carrying off a victim into the night.
It was one of six witchcraft paintings bought by the Duke and Duchess of Osuna.
And the picture seems to agree.
One man hides under a blanket, and another covers his ears.
They wear the pointed caps of penitents.
According to one reading, Goya turned the religious tribunals' accusations back on themselves.
Their own actions become the superstition and ritual sacrifice.
And the donkey beside them is a symbol of ignorance.
It isn't a picture of witches.
It's a picture of the people who hunted them.
So who is really doing the devouring, the witches or the judges?

meta.title: The witches who wore the church's hats
meta.description: Witches' Flight was painted by Francisco Goya in 1798 for the Duke and Duchess of Osuna and is now in the Prado. The witches wear penitential coroza caps, and one reading sees the accusations of religious tribunals turned back on the accusers.
meta.question: The witches, or the judges?
